'''Vili Mladenov Lilkov''' is a Bulgarian physicist, politician, author, and basketball player. He is the deputy chairman of the [[Sofia City Council]] (2023 - 2027) from the "Blue Sofia" coalition. In 2024, he founded the [[Blue Bulgaria]] coalition.

He is a professor at the [[Sofia University of Mining and Geology]]. Lilkov is also a co-founder of the [[Democrats for a Strong Bulgaria]]. He served four terms as a member of the Sofia City Council (1999–2014) and was deputy chairman (2011–2014) representing the [[Union of Democratic Forces (Bulgaria)|Union of Democratic Forces]] and the [[Blue Coalition]]. He was a member of the [[43rd National Assembly of Bulgaria|43rd National Assembly]] as part of the [[Reformist Bloc]] parliamentary group.

== Early life and education ==
Vili Lilkov graduated from the local High School of physics and mathematics. After winning the selection round at the [[International Physics Olympiad]], he was admitted without any examination to [[Sofia University]] in 1973. He graduated with a degree in [[Engineering Physics]] and a specialization in [[Nuclear Physics]] in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |last=dimitar |date=2018-02-03 |title=Вили Младенов Лилков |url=https://vidin-almanac.bg/%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BB%D0%B8-%D0%BC%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2-%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BB%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2/ |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Видински АЛМАНАХ |language=bg-BG}}</ref>

He would work at the Chemical Plant in Vidin from 1980 to 1983.

== Scientific career ==
He joined the Department of Physics of the [[Sofia University of Mining and Geology]] (1984) as an assistant, became a senior assistant (1986), then a chief assistant (1988). He was a part-time PhD student in [[Neutron (physics)|neutron physics]] at the Institute of Nuclear Research and Nuclear Energy of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] under the supervision of prof. Kiril Krejov in 1989–1994. He defended his doctoral thesis on "Spectrometer for polarized neutrons and study of amorphous magnetic bands" in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://mgu.bg/cv/CV_MGU_BG_VMLilkov.pdf | title=Вили младенов лилков | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003222340/http://mgu.bg/cv/CV_MGU_BG_VMLilkov.pdf | archive-date=3 October 2015 | language=bg | trans-title=Villas Mladenov Lilkov}}</ref>

He became Associate Professor (1998), then Professor (2011) of [[Nuclear Physics]] at the Sofia University of Mining and Geology. Since 1999 he has been Head of the Department of Physics and is currently a lecturer in general physics and atomic and nuclear physics at the university.

In 2018, he defended his dissertation on "Hydration of cements with mineral additives and structure of hardened cement pastes" and received the degree of Doctor of Science.

== Political career ==
In 1994 he became a member of the [[Union of Democratic Forces (Bulgaria)|Union of the Democratic Forces]] and then chairman of its regional organization in the capital's [[Triaditsa, Sofia|Triaditsa district]]. He was a co-founder of the [[Democrats for a Strong Bulgaria]] party (2004) and became chairman of its [[Sofia]] city organization in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Избраха Николай Стойнев и Вили Лилков за зам. – председатели на Столичния общински съвет – Политика |url=https://novini.bg/bylgariya/politika/31674 |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Novini.bg |language=bg}}</ref>

In 1999 he was elected to the [[Sofia City Council]] and served for 4 consecutive terms. In 2011, he was elected Deputy Chairman of the Sofia Cith Council.

At the [[2014 Bulgarian parliamentary election|parliamentary elections in October 2014]] he became a member of the XLIII [[National Assembly]] as part of the [[Reformist Bloc]] parliamentary group.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2014-10-10 |title=ЦИК обяви новите депутати, 19 са избрани с преференция |url=https://www.dnevnik.bg/bulgaria/2014/10/10/2397534_cik_obiavi_novite_deputati_19_sa_izbrani_s_preferenciia/ |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}}</ref>

In September 2015, Lilkov was the candidate of the [[Reformist Bloc]] for [[List of mayors of Sofia|Mayor of Sofia]]. He finished second and received 9.62% of the votes but the [[GERB]] candidate [[Yordanka Fandakova]] was still re-elected as mayor in the first round of the election by reaching a majority result of 60.17%.<ref>{{cite web | title=Местни избори :: Местни избори и национален референдум 2015 | url=https://results.cik.bg/minr2015/tur1/mestni/2246.html }}</ref>

In 2021, he joined the initiative committee that nominated [[Anastas Gerdzhikov]] for [[President of Bulgaria]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-10-05 |title=Инфографика: Профилът на хората от инициативния комитет на Анастас Герджиков |url=https://boulevardbulgaria.bg/articles/infografika-profilat-na-horata-ot-initsiativniya-komitet-na-anastas-gerdzhikov |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=boulevardbulgaria.bg |language=bg}}</ref>

On 15 July 2023, an initiative committee nominated Lilkov for [[List of mayors of Sofia|Mayors of Sofia]]. He went on to accept the invitation and join the race.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-15 |title=Популярен учен и изследовател в битката за кмет на София, ето кой е той |url=https://dariknews.bg/novini/bylgariia/populiaren-uchen-i-izsledovatel-v-bitkata-za-kmet-na-sofiia-eto-koj-e-toj-2353333 |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=dariknews.bg |language=bg}}</ref> His candidacy heavily opposed [[PP-DB]] candidate [[Vasil Terziev]], whose controversial family background was criticized by Lilkov. He also declared himself in opposition to the governing model of [[GERB]], the party that had been in charge of Sofia for the past 18 years. He also claimed to be the only right wing candidate in the race. He received the full support of the [[Conservative Union of the Right]] party, led by [[Petar Moskov]]. Together, they launched the "Blue Sofia" project calling, for the support of other right wing parties like the [[Union of the Democratic Forces (Bulgaria)|Union of the Democratic Forces]] and [[Democrats for Strong Bulgaria]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-01 |title=Вили Лилков и Петър Москов влизат в коалиция "Синя София" за местните избори |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/15027837 |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=www.24chasa.bg |language=en}}</ref> The first decided to remain a part of the local coalition [[GERB-SDS]] and so did the second by remaining a member of [[Democratic Bulgaria]].

Lilkov ended up fifth in the [[2023 Sofia mayoral election|election]] with 21,326 votes, which represents 5.69% of the total votes cast.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | title=Резултати :: Местни избори 29 октомври 2023 | url=https://results.cik.bg/mi2023/tur1/rezultati/2246.html }}</ref> He refused to endorse a candidate for the second round of the election between [[Vasil Terziev]] and [[Vanya Grigorova]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-01 |title=Вили Лилков не е нито за Терзиев, нито за Григорова на балотажа в София |url=https://www.segabg.com/hot/category-bulgaria/vili-lilkov-ne-e-nito-za-terziev-nito-za-grigorova-na-balotazha-sofiya |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Новини СЕГА |language=bg}}</ref> Nevertheless, his result granted him and his party 3 seats at the [[Sofia City Council]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Books ==
Lilkov has thoroughly researched archival documents relating to Bulgaria's recent past. He was author or co-author of the following books:

* ''Former People'' (2017)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-16 |title=Представят книгата |url=https://dariknews.bg/regioni/dobrich/predstaviat-knigata-bivshi-hora-razkrivashta-represiite-na-komunisticheskata-vlast-2125812 |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=dariknews.bg |language=bg}}</ref>
* ''The Ruined Bulgaria'' (2019)<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2019-05-16 |title=Над 500 души на премиерата на "Погубената България" от проф. Вили Лилков и Христо Христoв |url=https://ciela.bg/2019/05/novini/nad-500-dushi-na-premierata-na-pogubenata-balgariya-ot-prof-vili-lilkov-i-hristo-hristov/ |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Ciela |language=bg-BG}}</ref>
* ''Valor and Punishment'' (2021)
* ''The Economic Absurdities of Bulgarian Communism'' (2022)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-08 |title=Стопанските абсурди на българския комунизъм събра в книга Вили Лилков |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/stopanskite-absurdi-na-balgarskiya-komunizam-sabra-v-kniga-vili-lilkov-news334361.html |access-date=2023-11-02 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}}</ref>
* ''Our People'' (2023)
